title: Captions Disappear on Bright Shots? Check Contrast in Motion
description: Choose captions that stay readable across bright skies, windows and busy shots. Preview styles on iPhone and inspect the saved captioned video.
direct: Choose captions that stay readable when the background changes. Watch the brightest and busiest parts of the video at phone size before exporting.
figureAlt: The same bright scene uses white caption text first without a backing and then with a dark backing.
figureCaption: AI-generated typography example. Only the caption backing changes; this is not an App screenshot or export comparison.
cards.decision.heading: Play through cuts
cards.decision.body: Check moving footage, not only a paused title frame. Tree branches, patterned clothing and quick scene cuts can make a previously clear style difficult to read.
sections.detail-0-0.heading: Contrast needs a stable edge
sections.detail-0-0.body: The W3C’s media accessibility requirements identify thicker outlines or shadows as ways to improve contrast against video. A contrasting backing can also separate words from changing scenery. The figure demonstrates that typography principle; it is not a claim about a particular app style or a measured export.
sections.detail-1-0.heading: Choose from the styles you have
sections.detail-1-0.body: It includes clean subtitles, word highlights, animated styles and editable text. Some styles require Pro, and free single-video exports include the app watermark.
sections.detail-1-1.heading: Switch styles if words disappear
sections.detail-1-1.body: This guide does not promise separate controls for every outline, shadow or background parameter. If a chosen style disappears in part of the scene, try another available style and repeat the preview. The task is styling your new captions, not removing or restyling text already burned into another video. Readability checks alone do not certify accessibility compliance.
faqs.reader-question-1.heading: Is white text enough on a bright window shot?
faqs.reader-question-1.body: Look for a style with clearer separation from the background, such as a visible edge or dark backing when available. Check it in motion.
faqs.reader-question-2.heading: Why should I check the saved file with the audio muted?
faqs.reader-question-2.body: Without speech to fill in missed words, disappearing captions are easier to notice. Check quick cuts and the actual upload preview as well.

steps.step-1.text: Generate captions in Subtitle Maker: Just Captions and correct the transcript. Start with a clear style before adding word highlights or decorative animation.
steps.step-2.text: Preview passages with the brightest and busiest backgrounds at normal phone size. Compare available styles and prefer one whose lettering stays distinct across those passages.
steps.step-3.text: Export the captioned video and watch the saved copy with sound muted. Check both fast speech and scene changes, then inspect the actual upload preview before publishing.
